title: LyricWare enterprise outbound crib
body:
Quick brain-dump for LyricWare outbound / partnership exploration. Use this as the working scratchpad — will refine into a short one-pager and pilot proposal after sync with Ibrahim and Solutions.

1) One-line thesis about fit
- LyricWare = mid-market enterprise focused on customer support automation and content ingestion (multimodal docs). Their backlog mentions slow user search relevancy and high annotation cost. Redwood fits as an inference layer for faster, cheaper semantic search + private deployments for sensitive customer documents.

2) What I found (fast notes from site / investor deck / job posts)
- HQ: Denver, ~850 employees, B2B SaaS (support + knowledge management).
- Recent hiring: VP of Infra, Senior ML engineer (search/ranking), compliance lead (indicates regulated customers).
- Product notes: emphasis on "data privacy" and "on-prem connectors"; enterprise customers in healthcare and finance listed as references.
- Pricing: usage + seat model; current partners mention slow inference costs when scaling embeddings.

3) Key pain hypotheses to test in outreach
- Cost/latency bottleneck for semantic search at scale (batch job inference / realtime retrieval).
- Need for private deployment options to satisfy regulated customers (HIPAA, finance).
- Ops overhead for model rollouts across environments (dev/staging/prod).

4) Redwood value props to highlight (short bullets for email/call)
- Production-grade inference: 2–5x lower per-token cost via batching + KV cache for doc search workloads.
- Deployment flexibility: quick hosted POC, Dedicated reserved capacity for predictable throughput, Private VPC/on-prem for regulated pipelines.
- Observability & guardrails: token-level cost breakdown, evals tied to prompt sets to guard model regressions.
- Fast pilot: can spin a small dedicated pool and run a 4-week pilot with a quantifiable cost/latency baseline.

5) Outbound sequence (subject lines / snippets)
- Email 1 (intro): Subject: "Pilot idea to cut search inference cost at LyricWare"
  Snippet: "Short note — we’ve helped product teams reduce semantic-search token spend by ~45% without accuracy loss. Quick 20-min chat to share the approach?"
- Email 2 (follow): Subject: "Example: 40% cost drop + private deployment for health customers"
  Snippet: "We can run a short pilot against a snapshot of your doc store (no data leaves your VPC). Low lift + measurable savings."
- LinkedIn InMail: brief value + ask for intro to ML/Infra lead.

6) Likely objections & rebuttals (prep cues for SDR/AE)
- Objection: "We already have embeddings infra — why switch?"
  Rebuttal: "Most teams keep embeddings but pay 2–4x on inference due to no batching/prefix caching. Our runtime sits behind existing model outputs and reduces per-query compute without changing downstream UX. We also provide rollout controls and quantization options for unit-cost wins."
- Objection: "Security/privacy concerns — we can’t share customer data."
  Rebuttal: "We support Private deployments and VPC-only control planes (HSM/KMS integrations). Pilot can run inside your VPC with no data egress — proposed legal checklist for SAC review included."
- Objection: "Migration/engineering effort is too high."
  Rebuttal: "We provide SDKs + a short integration kit (node/python) and a Solutions engineer to pair-program the first routes; typical POC is 1–2 sprints for a single retrieval path."

7) Pilot idea (4-week guardrailed experiment)
- Week 0: Kickoff + baseline capture (latency, p95/p99, token cost per query).
- Week 1–2: Deploy a small Dedicated pool or Private demo in a sandbox; migrate 1 retrieval route (kb search). Enable smart prefix caching and batching for that route.
- Week 3: Run side-by-side A/B test vs current infra; collect latency/cost/quality metrics.
- Week 4: Review + decide scaled rollout or rollback.
- Success criteria: >=30% reduction in per-query spend while p99 latency stays within 1.5x baseline and no significant drop in retrieval relevance (measured by existing eval set).

8) Pricing sketch for pilot (internal, very rough)
- Hosted POC: free credits up to $X for 2 weeks + engineering support (low-friction).
- Dedicated short-term pilot: $Y/day for a small GPU pool (covering reserved capacity for the experiment) — include credits toward first month if move to committed.
- Private (on-prem/VPC): fixed setup fee + monthly platform license in enterprise deals (negotiate separately).

9) Ask for first call 
- Target: Intro with ML infra or Head of Product (search). Ask: 20–30 min to share pilot plan + baseline questions.
- Proposed Slack/Intro msg: "Hi <Name> — I’m Maya with Redwood Inference. We help search teams cut inference costs and standardize private deployments. Can I share a 4-week pilot plan that runs in your VPC and aims to reduce token spend by ~30%?"

10) Notes for the follow-up one-pager (to produce after sync)
- Short summary of problem + pilot approach, technical appendix (SDK snippet + sample rollout policy), security checklist (KMS/HSM, audit logs), commercial headline (pilot pricing + next-step path to Dedicated).

Random scraps / convo points to remember
- Ask about their eval datasets and how they measure retrieval relevance (A/B? nDCG?).
- Confirm whether embeddings are served centrally or generated at ingestion time (affects cache strategy).
- Check if any managed partners already in their stack (e.g., Pinecone, Weaviate) — call out migration story.

——
Next actions (my personal todo):
- Clean this into a 1-pager + 3-email sequence by 2026-02-24.
- Schedule 30-min prep with Ibrahim for technical script and sample SDK snippet.
- Draft pilot SOW template to attach if they ask for costs.

End of crib — quick and messy. Will tidy after first internal review.
